# Dodona

> A voice-native decision model. Ask typed questions about speech — yes/no,
> multiple choice, ordinal scale — and get calibrated probabilities read
> straight from the audio. No transcript in between, and no text is generated.

## Start here

- [Model on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/bahadobay/dodona-audio): 46
  calibrated questions, full calibration and reliability tables, benchmark
  results against Qwen2-Audio, and a model card stating what it can and cannot
  answer.
- [Code on GitHub](https://github.com/bahadobay/dodona-audio): Python API and
  MCP server. Apache-2.0, weights included.
- [Examples](https://github.com/bahadobay/dodona-audio/blob/main/EXAMPLES.md):
  real outputs on real recordings, with the audio each one comes from named.

## Use it

- [MCP server](https://github.com/bahadobay/dodona-audio#use-it-from-claude-mcp):
  add `dodona-mcp` to an MCP client to let an assistant ask questions about
  audio files. Runs locally and needs a CUDA GPU of about 24 GB.
- Install with
  `pip install git+https://github.com/bahadobay/dodona-audio`.

## What it is good at

- How something was said: emotion, tone, speaking rate, hesitation.
- Who is speaking: number of speakers, overlapping speech, laughter.
- Whether a specific word was said, including words never seen in training,
  with a calibrated probability.

## Limits

- Trained on English speech. Emotion was learned from actors, and scales such
  as speaking rate are weak.
- A yes/no answer describes the recording's strongest 10-second window, not the
  whole recording; `where` says which window. Choice and score answers are
  averaged over the windows.
- It is not a chat model. Dodona answers questions about audio; it does not hold
  a conversation.
- Every answer carries a `status`: `calibrated`, `not verified`, or
  `off catalogue`. Only the first means the probability can be relied on.
